title: Prime Split: 4-day Distributed Full-Body
author: Matt Ladewig
desc:
PURPOSE
A minimalist full-body program distributed over four days for the full gym. Built for limited time, it uses four short sessions to develop strength and muscle through quality reps, manageable fatigue, and clear progression.

WHO IT’S FOR
Novice to early-intermediate lifters who want a routine built around controlled ROM, appropriate effort, consistent technique, and measurable progress.

REQUIREMENTS
• Full gym
• 4 sessions per week
• 30–40 minutes per session

SCHEDULE
Train four days weekly. Example:
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday.

METHODOLOGY

1. CONTROLLED RANGE OF MOTION
Use the largest pain-free range you can control consistently. Keep setup, depth, posture, and movement path repeatable. End the set when ROM shortens, posture breaks down, momentum takes over, or another clean rep is unlikely.

2. INTENSITY CONTROL
Week 1 is for load calibration—not failure testing. Choose weights that leave 2–3 reps in reserve.

During Weeks 2–8, perform work sets around RPE 8, or about 2 reps in reserve. Avoid grinders and routine failure. Isolation exercises may occasionally reach RPE 9 on the final set if technique remains clean.

3. DOUBLE PROGRESSION
Stay within the prescribed rep range. Add reps while maintaining clean technique and target RPE. When all work sets reach the top of the range, increase the load and return toward the lower end.

Use the smallest practical increase. If a 5 lb jump per dumbbell is too large, continue building reps first.

4. STIMULUS-TO-FATIGUE PRIORITY
   Exercises are selected for high return per set. Unilateral leg work reduces dumbbell loading limits, while bench-supported rows reduce lower-back fatigue. Rows provide strong horizontal pulling but do not fully replace pull-ups or pulldowns.

5. STANDARDIZE EXECUTION
   Keep bench angle, stance, grip, ROM, technique, and rest periods consistent. Do not change technique simply to record more reps.

BENCH ANGLES
• Incline press: 20–30°
• Incline curl: 45–60°
• Rear-delt fly: 30–45°
• Seated shoulder press: 75–85°, ribs down

REST
• Compound lifts: 2–3 minutes
• Isolation exercises: 60–90 seconds
Rest long enough to preserve load, reps, ROM, and technique.

WARM-UP
Perform 3–5 minutes of movement and 1–3 progressively heavier preparation sets before the first major exercise.

VOLUME ADJUSTMENT
Run the program as written for 8 weeks. If progress stalls for 2–3 weeks, first review sleep, nutrition, heat, rest, technique, and load increments. If recovery is good, add one set to one exercise per session—not every exercise.

PRIMARY RULE
Progress comes from repeatable, high-quality work and gradual improvement—not from making every workout maximal.
